dimensions.explanation: The route attaches to applications and submissions concerning IPD-administered investment products. Submitters are identified by activity, not an expressly specified licence or institutional class. The launch context includes new applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions; it does not support a new-cases-only exception.

Footnote 1 supplies product categories but does not define their boundaries. Footnote 2 expands WINGS as Web-based INteGrated Service. Reading WINGS2 as WINGS with a footnote marker is supported by that pairing; independent typography is unavailable.

No express post-cutover routing exception appears. Where practicable attaches to SFC review and enhancement, not submitter routing. Parallel-run acceptance is temporal, not grandfathering for cases opened during that period. Missing integration timing does not establish a legacy-system exemption. Exceptions in unavailable material remain unresolved.

Must establishes mandatory routing. Can also permits annual-fee settlement through e-IP; the full-adoption heading does not make that payment route mandatory. SFC statements about extension, integration and enhancement announce administrative actions. Contacting case officers is an invitation, not a prerequisite or waiver procedure.

Launch was 29 July 2024. The extension replaces the initial 29 October endpoint with 29 November 2024; mandatory routing starts 30 November 2024. Continued existing-channel acceptance during the extended month is inferred from extending the parallel run. Treatment of filings spanning cutover and independent integration or fee-function availability dates remain unspecified.

The 8 July 2024 launch circular is expressly referenced but unavailable. The packet's missing dependency identifier is only provisionally associated with it. Its definitions, procedures and exceptions cannot be imported. The supplied text supports the bounded routing proposal, not complete treatment across related authority.

Extending the parallel run carries forward existing-channel acceptance through 29 November 2024. This inference is not necessary to evaluate the selected post-cutover control.

citations.quote: After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing.
In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable.

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.
Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024

readings.distinction: Retain one supported reading. Attaching where practicable to routing would excuse impracticable e-IP use, but the phrase qualifies a different actor and action: SFC review and enhancement. Grandfathering would spare later filings in existing cases, but acceptance is stated for a period, not a cohort. Deferring legacy-report routing until separately confirmed integration would add an unstated exception. Mandatory annual-fee routing would contradict the permissive can also wording. These hypotheses lack sufficient source support for rival formalizations. The strongest uncertainty is whether the unavailable launch circular supplies transitional or operational qualifications. The parent fact definitions and expression are preserved; null diagnostic snapshots provide no concrete counterexample.
